title: Datasets for classification and regression in human-robot interaction with parallel robots
author: Aran Mohammad

queries: robot physical interaction contact onset ground truth skin collision dataset foam force sensor external FSR robot timestamp data ground truth collision data download contact times
Dataset landing → all three CKAN ZIPs and READMEs → companion DOI/arXiv, acquisition §IV-A and experiments, Figures 4 and 6.
grade: Real planar parallel robot. Six-axis KMS40 sensor mounted successively on specific links or the platform, manual contact force applied to the sensor. Independent sensing physics from the model-based momentum observer; joint/external platform forces projected from the sensor are transformations of that same measurement, not additional sensors.
scope: All 3 original CKAN ZIPs, 5 CSVs, 760,307 published rows. Raw F/T and the projected reference are present in both collided-body splits and the regression file. Contact-type train/test (136,416 rows) lack those measurements. No per-row independent electrical first-touch label. Acquisition and software used 1 kHz; the time column in the training and testing exports has jumps and resets.
cleaning: Check all columns for nonfinite values, time reversals and missing 1ms steps. Analyze reference/estimate pairs for elapsed times within continuous runs only. Compare the components of the projected platform wrench in base coordinates; x and y in N, last component is a moment in Nm. Group residuals by body within original split. Do not pool force and moment units.
timing: Restrict event comparison to the nine unbroken 1-ms stretches of the regression file, each with constant chain/link/location. Compare norms of planar projected forces at thresholds 2/5/10 N. A rise requires 1/5/10 consecutive observations on each side of the threshold. Pair only mutually unique same-segment crossings within ±100 ms. These analyst-defined events are neither contact-onset ground truth nor a reproduction of paper detection accuracy. They can include multiple crossings within a single physical contact.
findings: At 5 N, raising persistence from 1 to 5 to 10 points per side changes the sensor count from 94 to 44 to 42; the observer counts are 2,363, 24 and 2. The measurement onset rule strongly affects counts on identical records.
reproduce: Python + numpy/pandas. Obtain the 3 listed original ZIPs into INPUT_DIR named classification_body.zip, classification_type.zip and regression_location_force.zip; run python derive_parallel.py INPUT_DIR OUT.
